@@ -49,6 +50,17 @@ The default maximum time range for a metrics query is 24 hours, configured using
This is different to the default TraceQL maximum time range of 168 hours (7 days).
+`max_duration` gives every tenant the same range, but data volume differs by orders of magnitude between tenants.

+Use `query_frontend.metrics.max_scanned_bytes` to limit a query by the bytes of the backend blocks it scans. It allows users to the query for time ranges between `min_duration` and `max_duration` and scans data upto `max_scanned_bytes`.
+A query of `min_duration` or less is always allowed, and a longer query over the allowed range is rejected with a 400 error. `min_duration` must not be above `max_duration`.
+Only backend blocks count toward `max_scanned_bytes`, so data newer than `query_backend_after` isn't counted.
+The limit counts the requested range, so step alignment can add up to 4 steps of data on top of `max_scanned_bytes`.
The `query_frontend.metrics.query_backend_after` parameter controls the boundary between querying the live-store and backend storage.
@@ -40,6 +40,64 @@ As jobs complete, new ones are dispatched.
This limits the blast radius of a single large query.
In shared clusters, keeping this value lower ensures fair scheduling across tenants.
+`max_duration` gives every tenant the same range, but the same range can hold gigabytes for one tenant and terabytes for another.
+`max_scanned_bytes`, under `query_frontend.search` or `query_frontend.metrics`, limits the range by the bytes of the backend blocks it scans.
+The allowed range is the longest window ending at the query end whose backend blocks fit in `max_scanned_bytes`.
+It's then raised to `min_duration` and capped at `max_duration`.
+Longer queries are rejected with a 400 error that reports the allowed range.
+A query of `min_duration` or less is always allowed. A query longer than `max_duration` is always rejected with the `max_duration` error, before `max_scanned_bytes` is checked.

+Tempo fails to start if `min_duration` is above `max_duration`. A per-tenant overrides reload fails if a tenant sets `min_search_duration` above `max_search_duration`, or `min_metrics_duration` above `max_metrics_duration`, and Tempo keeps the last valid overrides. If the overrides are invalid at startup, Tempo fails to start. If a tenant override and the `query_frontend` value give a `min_duration` above `max_duration`, `max_duration` wins.

+Metrics queries are counted over the requested range. Step alignment can widen the scanned range by up to 4 steps, so a query with a large step can scan more than `max_scanned_bytes`, the same as with `max_duration`.
+`0` (default) disables the limit, and `min_duration` has no effect without `max_scanned_bytes`.
+For example, this configuration lets a search span up to 30 days when its blocks fit in 500 GB,
+Per-tenant overrides replace these values for one tenant.
+set under `read` in the per-tenant overrides file.
+Each tenant of a multi-tenant metrics query is checked against its own limits, including its own `max_metrics_duration`, so the query gets the lowest limit of its tenants.
+To calibrate, when `max_scanned_bytes` is set, the frontend logs a `msg="scanned bytes limit"` line for each tenant a query checks, including queries that `max_duration` rejects.
+A query of `min_duration` or less isn't checked, so it isn't logged.
+Each line has `estimated_scanned_bytes`, the estimated bytes the requested range scans, next to `max_scanned_bytes`, so the gap shows how far to raise the limit for that query.
+To turn the limit on without rejecting any query allowed today, set `min_duration` to the current `max_duration`.
+With that setting, only queries over `max_duration` are logged. The LogQL query below reads those lines.
+A tenant with a `max_search_duration` or `max_metrics_duration` override also needs `min_search_duration` or `min_metrics_duration` set to the same value.
+Otherwise, ranges between the config `min_duration` and the tenant's `max_duration` are limited by `max_scanned_bytes`.
+This LogQL query lists queries of 7 days or less that `max_duration` rejects, but whose estimated bytes fit a `max_scanned_bytes` of 200 GB:
+{namespace="tempo", container="query-frontend"} |= "scanned bytes limit" | logfmt | result="rejected_max_duration" | requested_seconds <= 604800 | estimated_scanned_bytes <= 200000000000
Queriers connect to the query frontend over streaming gRPC.
